subject: DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer — train fleet telemetry (Greenhouse 8432987002)
paragraphs: I am writing about the DevOps / Cloud Infrastructure Engineer engagement that connects the new train fleet to Flix's cloud platform. The part of the description that matters most to me is the smallest sentence in it: knowing what is happening in the systems before the users do. That is the problem I have spent three years solving on a smaller fleet, and it is telemetry and closed-loop alerting, not dashboards.

I run thirteen Linux hosts from one declaration. A sentinel collects job status, generation age, disk pressure and PSI from every host every fifteen minutes, writes it to a ledger, and raises a page on any state that is not ok; the alert closes when the state changes, not when someone acknowledges it. Machines are provisioned over PXE and iVentoy, join the declaration on first boot and rebuild from it, which is the same shape as bringing a device onto a fleet and keeping it honest remotely. Secrets and certificates are per host — SOPS/age, an in-house certificate authority with short-lived certificates — and networking is nftables default-deny with DNS, MTU and TLS faults read from tcpdump and openssl.

Where I would have to learn: I have not used Terraform or Terragrunt, and infrastructure as code in my work is Nix rather than HCL — the concepts of pinned providers, state and reviewed plans are familiar, the tool is not. My AWS experience is a small Lambda project rather than platform ownership, and I have run Oracle Cloud hosts but not designed a multi-account estate. I have built certificate management and TLS, but not mTLS as a service-to-service policy layer, and I have never integrated an IoT or automotive device fleet or worked in the JVM ecosystem. Those are real gaps and I would rather name them than have them found in week two.

On the contract: I am based in Germany and open to the B2B service-agreement model; I would need to confirm whether an existing entity can invoice Flix or whether a Polish entity has to be set up. I am not currently based in Poland, so the honest answer to that question is no, and I would need a Polish residence and work permit if the engagement requires presence — I would take that on for the right scope, or work remotely from Germany if the collaboration allows it. Rate: the band of 90–119 PLN/hour is below what I charge, so I would ask for 150 PLN/hour net, or a narrower scope at the top of your band.

What I can offer on day one is the operating discipline: measure first, alert on state, provision by declaration, keep the rollback one step away, and write the runbook the next engineer needs at 02:00. I would welcome a technical conversation about the onboard-to-cloud boundary — that is where the interesting decisions are.
